title: I Hate the Tempter and His Charms
description: I Hate the Tempter and His Charms in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 7 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 156, headed “Presumption and despair; or, Satan's various temptations”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: I hate the temp-ter and his charms, I hate his flat-tering breath; The ser-pent takes a thou-sand forms To cheat our souls to death.

lines: I hate the tempter and his charms,
The serpent takes a thousand forms
To cheat our souls to death.
He feeds our hopes with airy dreams,
And holds us still in wide extremes,
Anon he swells our sins, and cries,
He tells the aged, "They must die,
"In vain for mercy now they cry,
Thus he supports his cruel throne
And drags the sons of Adam down
Almighty God, cut short his power,
And, that he vex the earth no more,

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
